feature: GitHub and Azure DevOps backlog triage
summary: Replace the GitHub-only triage skill with one `ai-triage` entry point that preserves GitHub behavior and adds safe, complete Azure DevOps Services reports. Each run resolves one scope, reads without remote mutations, and writes a full report only when its inventory is complete.
plain_summary: People can get one complete, ranked backlog report from GitHub or Azure DevOps without changing anything in either service.
gating: Work checkpoints in order. Within a checkpoint, the gates run in order: behavior, then ui, then review. A checkpoint is "passed" only when every gate is "passed" or "n/a". Do not start checkpoint N+1 until checkpoint N has passed.

checkpoints.title: Unify the skill and preserve GitHub triage
checkpoints.goal: The branch PRD records the approved ai-triage scope, one public skill preserves the existing GitHub inventory, ranking, evidence and read-only behavior, the old skill is retired, and the replacement is bundled.

plain.what: People still get the same complete GitHub backlog report from one renamed skill.
plain.why: Without this, the new name could silently lose details people already rely on.
plain.check: Run the GitHub fixture and confirm every expected item and report section remains.

tasks: Sync `.ai-engineering/PRD.html` on this feature branch with the approved decisions from `.ai-engineering/brainstorm.html`; the branch baseline PRD has no ai-triage scope.

Create `skills/ai-triage/SKILL.md` as the single shared entry point and move the existing GitHub procedure into `skills/ai-triage/references/github.md`; preserve its issue and pull-request inventories, pagination, per-item analysis, ranking, evidence, report contract, and read-only boundary.

Retire `skills/ai-github-triage/` only after the new provider reference and regression fixture are in place; do not add an alias. Until Azure support is complete, an Azure route must stop before any remote read.

Add `tests/triage-github.spec.ts` with synthetic GitHub issue/PR fixtures that exercise the replacement route and assert complete inventory, preserved report sections and fields, item linkage, and no remote writes.
Regenerate `src/assets.ts` with `bun scripts/gen-assets.ts` and verify the new skill and provider reference are embedded while the retired skill is absent.
acceptance: The PRD contains the approved single-skill replacement and GitHub-preservation decisions without changing unrelated product scope.
A synthetic GitHub run keeps every issue and pull request visible, including unassessed items, and preserves the existing ranking, evidence and report behavior.
Only `ai-triage` is the public skill name; `skills/ai-github-triage/` is gone and an Azure target fails closed before reading.
`bun test tests/skills.spec.ts` and `bun test tests/embed-canon.spec.ts` prove the new skill is valid and embedded, with no retired skill payload.

checkpoints.title: Resolve Azure targets before reading
checkpoints.goal: A deterministic resolver chooses an explicit URL's provider and scope or a unique repository remote, and returns an ambiguity that must be answered before any Azure request.

plain.what: The skill knows which Azure project and board to read, or asks before opening anything.
plain.why: Guessing from the signed-in account could expose the wrong team's private backlog.
plain.check: Try clear and ambiguous URLs and remotes; ambiguous cases must make no read call.

tasks: Add `skills/ai-triage/scripts/resolve-target.mjs` to resolve explicit GitHub or Azure DevOps Services URLs before remotes, and otherwise derive only the provider and project scope established by repository remotes.
Return an explicit needs-answer result when provider, project, team, board or backlog level is ambiguous; have `skills/ai-triage/SKILL.md` ask before reading and retain any answer only for that run.
Require explicit Azure organization and project arguments downstream; reject Azure DevOps Server and never inspect active `az` defaults or add a triage field to `.ai-engineering/config.toml`.
Add `tests/triage-routing.spec.ts` using synthetic URLs and remotes, plus a fake request adapter that proves ambiguous and unsupported targets trigger zero reads.
acceptance: An explicit URL fixes provider and scope even when repository remotes disagree.
Without a URL, only one unambiguous remote determines provider/project; missing or conflicting provider, project or board information asks before any read.
Azure Services targets carry explicit organization and project values; no active Azure CLI default or persisted config field supplies scope.
Synthetic tests cover GitHub and Azure URLs, unique and conflicting remotes, missing board selection, unsupported Azure Server, and zero reads on ambiguity.

checkpoints.title: Collect a complete read-only Azure backlog
checkpoints.goal: The selected Azure backlog level yields a complete, normalized inventory of nonterminal work items using process-aware state categories, bounded batch reads and a provable completion condition; otherwise collection fails closed.

plain.what: The report receives every eligible item from one board, with related parents or children only as context.
plain.why: A capped or guessed list could hide work and make the ranking misleading.
plain.check: Synthetic large backlogs must finish completely or report failure, never a smaller complete-looking list.

tasks: Add `skills/ai-triage/scripts/collect-azure.mjs` and `skills/ai-triage/references/azure-devops.md` for Azure DevOps Services only; use explicit organization/project scope and one selected board/backlog level per run.

Discover work-item types and their process state categories; include every nonterminal category without hard-coded state names, and fetch parent/child links only for context without widening the inventory.

Define and enforce this default-deny `az devops invoke` allowlist with explicit `--organization`, project/team route parameters and API version: GET `/{project}/{team}/_apis/work/backlogs`; GET `/{project}/{team}/_apis/work/backlogs/{id}` when needed to resolve the selected level; GET `/{project}/_apis/wit/workitemtypes`; GET `/{project}/_apis/wit/workitemtypes/{type}/states`; POST `/{project}/_apis/wit/wiql`; POST `/{project}/_apis/wit/workitemsbatch`. Verify exact supported routes before implementation; add no other route/method pair without a documented read need and a pinned test.

Use `az devops invoke` only through the allowlist; do not use flat-only `az boards query` as a complete backlog read. Allow POST only for the listed read-only WIQL and batch endpoints, require explicit organization/project arguments, and cap each batch at 200 IDs.

Prove pagination/completeness before returning inventory; test continuation, empty final page, WIQL boundary, missing state metadata, API/auth errors and batches above 200 with sanitized synthetic fixtures in `tests/triage-azure.spec.ts`.
acceptance: The synthetic inventory contains every and only nonterminal item for the selected process-aware backlog level; parent/child context never adds inventory rows.

Every request matches an allowlisted method and route, carries explicit organization/project scope, and batch requests contain at most 200 IDs; no mutation-capable route or unbounded `invoke` is emitted.
A fixture crossing the supported WIQL/page boundary is complete only when the reader can prove all pages were fetched; an unknown or capped result fails rather than returning a complete flag.
Unknown process state categories, incomplete pagination, authentication failures and any non-allowlisted call stop collection without producing a report.
All Azure tests use synthetic fixtures; this checkpoint makes no tenant or authentication query.

checkpoints.title: Render complete Azure reports safely
checkpoints.goal: A complete Azure inventory becomes a full `.ai-engineering/triage.html` report using the shared artifact shell, Azure-appropriate sections, escaped untrusted content and validated HTTPS evidence; failures leave the previous report untouched.

plain.what: People can read the full Azure backlog, its ranking and useful related context in one safe page.
plain.why: A partial or unsafe page could hide work or run content copied from a work item.
plain.check: Open a synthetic report and confirm every item appears while hostile text stays inert.

tasks: Add `skills/ai-triage/scripts/render-report.mjs` and wire the shared router, Azure collector and report writer to `.ai-engineering/triage.html` only after routing and inventory completeness pass.

Reuse the existing shell and artifact design in `templates/triage.html.tpl`; render Azure-specific scope, ranked work, work-item types/states, related context and method sections rather than GitHub-only issue/PR sections.
Preserve per-item analysis for the complete inventory with no more than five analysts in flight, and show every item or an explicit `UNASSESSED` status instead of dropping unreviewed items.
Escape all untrusted Azure fields before HTML text or attributes; validate every evidence link as HTTPS before rendering and reject unsafe or malformed URLs.

Render fully before replacing the existing report; use sanitized synthetic fixtures in `tests/triage-report.spec.ts` to assert all rows/counts/linkages, Azure sections, hostile fields, invalid links and previous-report preservation on every failure path.
acceptance: A synthetic full run writes a complete HTML report to `.ai-engineering/triage.html` with Azure-specific sections inside the existing shared shell.
Every inventoried work item and its expected details/linkage is represented; report totals agree with inventory totals and related parent/child context does not inflate them.
Untrusted fields render as inert text, only validated HTTPS evidence links become links, and no authentication value is rendered.
No report is written or replaced after ambiguity, read, pagination, validation or render failure; an existing report remains byte-for-byte unchanged.
The shared shell/layout gates and synthetic report tests pass without reading or storing private Azure data.

checkpoints.title: Close documentation and verify the full feature
checkpoints.goal: Current documentation names only `ai-triage`, generated assets include the final shared and provider-specific procedures, and the complete GitHub/Azure suite and project gates pass without a private live report in the changes.

plain.what: People can find the new skill and understand what it reads and what it never changes.
plain.why: Outdated instructions could send people to a removed skill or imply Azure can be modified.
plain.check: Read the skill summary and run every project check before the feature is handed off.

tasks: Update the current skill listing in `README.md`, add the user-facing replacement/Azure Services entry to `CHANGELOG.md`, and update `FILEMAP.md` for the new skill structure; retain historical release entries as history.

Review `skills/ai-triage/SKILL.md` and provider references for one entry point, no alias, exact read-only Azure allowlist, explicit scope, per-run ambiguity answers, one-level inventory, five-agent cap, failure behavior and no configuration field.
Run `bun scripts/gen-assets.ts`, then verify `src/assets.ts` and embedded canon contain only the current skill paths.

Run the full suite and required project gates; optionally perform a live Azure smoke read only if separately authorized, using only allowlisted read calls, keeping raw/private output out of Git and never committing or pushing the live report.
acceptance: README and current instructions refer to `ai-triage`, not a separate `ai-github-triage` alias; changelog and file map match the final shipped structure.
The final embedded payload has the replacement skill and provider procedures and no retired skill folder.
`bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun test`, and `bun test tests/arch.spec.ts` all pass.
Automated checks use synthetic data only; no live private report or raw backlog output is added to Git, committed or pushed.

assumptions: Azure support means Azure DevOps Services only, not Azure DevOps Server. [Approved brainstorm, sections 8 and 11]

An explicit URL fixes provider and scope; repository remotes may resolve only what they identify, and ambiguous provider, project or board choices are asked per run. [Approved brainstorm, sections 6 and 8]

One Azure run inventories one selected backlog level, while parents and children are context only; each item keeps the GitHub analysis contract with at most five analysts in flight. [Approved feature decisions and existing GitHub procedure]
Azure state names vary by process, so terminal status is derived from discovered state categories rather than fixed names. [Approved feature decisions]
POST is allowed only for the explicitly named read-only WIQL and batch-read routes; broad `az devops invoke` access is not safe. [Approved Azure constraints]
If state discovery or pagination cannot prove a complete inventory, collection stops and the existing report stays unchanged. [Approved fail-closed and preserve-previous-report decisions]
Automated fixtures contain synthetic data only; a private real report is local output and never a committed or pushed artifact. [Approved brainstorm, sections 5 and 8]
The existing Bun toolchain is sufficient; no new dependency is needed unless implementation proves a required capability is absent. [AGENTS.md Project config and user instruction]
notes: The feature PRD is missing from this clean feature-branch baseline; synchronize it on this branch from the committed approved brainstorm before implementation, without changing the primary checkout.

Safe completeness beyond WIQL result limits and process-aware state-category discovery are technical risks, not permission to guess: if an implementation cannot prove completeness, it must fail closed and produce no partial report.
No Azure tenant or authentication query is part of planning or automated verification. A later live smoke read is optional and requires separate authorization; raw output stays out of Git.
No remote Azure mutation, multi-board aggregation, Azure DevOps Server support, persistent board configuration, commit or push of a live private report is in scope.
